chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who was in charge of the camels of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Najiya ibn Jundub Al-Khuzai Al-Aslamy, and the one who shaved the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him) during his Hajj was Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Haratha ibn Nasr ibn Awf ibn Aweij ibn Adi ibn Ka'b.

He (peace be upon him) said: And when it was the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he was shaving him, the Quraysh said, 'O Ma'mar! The ear of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is in your hand, and in your hand is the razor.' So Ma'mar said, 'By Allah! I count it as a great favor from Allah upon me.'

He (peace be upon him) said: And Ma'mar was the one who used to prepare the ride for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). So the Messenger of Allah said, 'O Ma'mar! The ride tonight is loose.' So Ma'mar said, 'By my father and my mother! I had tightened it just as I used to tighten it, but some of those who envy me for my place from you, O Messenger of Allah, intended that you would replace me.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'I would not have done it.'

key_terms.بُدْن: Camels used for sacrifice or transport

ai.seo_question: Who shaved the Prophet's head during his Hajj and what did he say about this honor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the honor bestowed upon Ma'mar ibn Abdullah for shaving the Prophet's head during the Farewell Hajj, illustrating the Shia emphasis on the virtue of those close to the Ahl al-Bayt. It further narrates a subtle incident where the Prophet's saddle loosened due to the envy of others, yet he remained steadfast in not replacing Ma'mar, demonstrating his patience and the enduring nature of divine favor despite worldly jealousy.
